dedupe_keys.name: china photovoltaic mapping random forest classifier

description: The China photovoltaic mapping research team publishes a Google Earth Engine classifier for mapping ground-mounted solar installations. The JavaScript source computes spectral indices, texture and terrain features from Sentinel-2 and ALOS inputs, then trains a random forest and checks an independent point split. It also applies a morphological filter to the classified image. Source access is public and free under MIT. The supplied example covers imagery from February to May 2020 within a user-defined region in China. Classification outputs can prepare photovoltaic asset locations for simulations alongside data-global-power-plant-database. A caveat is that the script expects imported boundary and training geometries that are absent from the GitHub tree. Sampling uses a 30-metre scale, which must be distinguished from the accompanying ten-metre map product. No Earth Engine execution or accuracy check was performed.
